questions.question: When a forwardable inner signature cannot be produced (locked/absent NIP-07 signer), is the meta-event truly not emitted — is there no code path where the relay-publish call still fires (e.g. with an empty/placeholder signature) while only the UI layer suppresses the error — and is local action (e.g. any local state update implying the send succeeded) also withheld, not just the network call?

Does the interactive-path error and the background/relay-path dev-log both live at the correct call boundary in MarmotContext.tsx / profileRequestHandler.ts (not duplicated ad hoc at each call site), and are the new user-facing error strings added to i18n.ts's `Copy` type plus both `en` and `de` objects (not hardcoded in the component), consumed via `useCopy()` per CLAUDE.md's translation rule?

Could `Profiles (forwarded)` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md?

Is there an integrated-e2e test (locked/absent signer, interactive user-initiated send) asserting a visible i18n-backed error appears, and a handler-unit test (background/relay send) asserting a dev-log-only failure with no UI error and continued reliance on the existing profile-request retry machinery — and do both tests assert on the *absence* of the meta-event (no relay publish call recorded), not just presence of the error path?

Does the background/relay failure path genuinely rely on the existing profile-request retry machinery (no new retry logic invented for this story), confirmed by tracing that the same retry code path already exercised elsewhere in profileRequestHandler.ts / profileRequestSync.ts is what picks up the failed send?

Does the signer-availability check happen before any partial local action (e.g. optimistic local application of the profile-request response, or a locally-cached 'sent' flag) is taken, so a failed send leaves no residual local state implying success?

Show the production code and both test levels proving AC-SEND-10: if a forwardable inner signature cannot be produced (locked/absent NIP-07 signer), the meta-event is not emitted and not actioned locally; an interactive send shows a visible, i18n-backed error (integrated-e2e); a background/relay send dev-logs the failure and relies on the existing retry machinery, showing no UI error (handler-unit) — confirm both paths are tested independently, not conflated into one assertion.

MarmotContext.tsx has FIVE call sites that produce a forwardable signed profile envelope (onHistorySynced auto-publish, sendSelfProfile's AC-030 self-reply, createGroup's welcome broadcast, inviteByNpub's post-invite re-send, publishProfileUpdate). This story classified only publishProfileUpdate as INTERACTIVE (visible error) and the other four as BACKGROUND/RELAY (dev-log only), on the reasoning that the other four are best-effort side effects of an already-successful primary action (group creation / invite / historical sync / an incoming request) rather than something the user is watching a 'send my profile' action for. Is this classification correct, or should createGroup's / inviteByNpub's profile broadcast — which DO fire synchronously inside a user-clicked action handler — also surface a visible error?

publishProfileUpdate had NO production caller anywhere in the app when this story started (confirmed by grepping app/src and app/pages before implementation) — the interactive path appeared to be dead code. Investigation found the real caller in app/pages/profile.tsx (handleNicknameBlur -> broadcastProfile -> publishProfileUpdate(next)), a file OUTSIDE this story's scope.includes. Does profile.tsx require ANY change for AC-SEND-10 to hold end-to-end (it does not call publishProfileUpdate expecting a specific return value or catch a rejection — the fail-closed contract is entirely internal to publishProfileUpdate itself), and is app/tests/e2e/groups-profile-send-fails-closed.spec.ts's decision to drive the REAL nickname-blur UI (rather than adding a synthetic window.__fewTest.publishProfileUpdate hook, which was implemented first and then removed once the real caller was found) the more faithful test per CLAUDE.md's 'publish through the app' rule?

onHistorySynced's profilePublishedRef Set previously marked a group 'already auto-published this session' BEFORE attempting serialiseProfileUpdate at all (a locally-cached optimistic 'sent' flag matching VQ-S8-006's exact failure pattern). This story moved the mark to occur ONLY after signAndSendProfileBackground reports { sent: true }. Was this pre-existing bug in-scope for AC-SEND-10 to fix (vs. a separate finding to file), and does the fix have any unintended effect on the 'exactly once per group per session' auto-publish intent the ref was originally added for (e.g. could a transient signing failure now cause the SAME group to be auto-published more than once per session if onHistorySynced's callback can fire more than once for the same group)?

There is no real NIP-07 browser extension in this repo's Playwright e2e harness (test identities use a local in-app signer seeded via localStorage, per auth-helpers.ts) — 'locked/absent NIP-07 signer' is simulated via a new dev-only window.__fewTest.forceProfileSignerFailure override on publishProfileUpdate, gated NODE_ENV !== 'production' and re-read on every call, mirroring authenticatedSenderResolver.ts's resolveAuthenticatedSender override precedent from S1. Is a synthetic override an acceptable substitute for a genuinely locked NIP-07 signer for THIS AC's e2e coverage, and does its narrow scope (affects only publishProfileUpdate, checked at call time, gated out of production builds) rule out any production risk?
